_readme: Machine-readable product contract. Read by tests/test_product_contract.py; explained in docs/product_contract.md. Status values: supported (qualified, acceptance tests exist), experimental (usable but not release-qualified; reason required), unavailable (not deliverable today; reason required), unqualified (outside the support claim). JSON rather than TOML because the project supports Python 3.10, where tomllib does not exist.

platforms.note: Only macOS arm64 carries release evidence for 1.2.x. doctor reports any other platform as NOT QUALIFIED (a warning, not a lie). The runtime wheel is macosx_11_0_arm64 only, so elsewhere the runtime floor cannot be satisfied and execution fails closed.

python.note: Each qualified version ran the full suite against the qualified runtime 49.0.4.post1+git.2c2970205f in its own venv, in CI shape (no packaged guest, no built wheel): 3.10.20, 3.11.15, 3.12.13 and 3.13.14 each 1809 passed / 31 skipped, rc=0 (measured 2026-10-23 on the 49.0.4 runtime; the per-run logs are the evidence) — STALE as of 2026-10-24: the v1.2 work added tests after that measurement, so the matrix numbers must be re-run before they are quoted again. The 3.12 canonical count in the same shape is now 2171 passed / 44 skipped (2215 collected). Each of those venvs has the package installed, because two legs exec the `ephemora` console script and examples/signed_record_demo.py as a subprocess. The split moves with what a venv carries - installed guest wheels turn three resolver legs from pass to skip (docs/release_assurance.md, states C/D) - so the per-run log is the evidence, not a constant. 3.14 is exercised as an interpreter guest only and carries no host claim. 3.10/3.11 needed a parser repair: CPython only intermixes a nargs='*' positional with optionals from 3.12.5 (gh-61252), so `run target --json a b` dropped the guest argv there - fixed in cli._parse_argv and pinned by tests/test_language_env_args_cli.py on every version.

capability.note: The patched 49.0.4 line (49.0.4.post1+git.2c2970205f, embedded dylib sha256 247c1529...a30b) is the only accepted runtime; the 49.0.3.post2 build is withdrawn for GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm. On macOS arm64 the execution gate hashes the exact native file the bindings load before any guest code executes and refuses a different file with error_class=environment; elsewhere only the version line is checked because no qualified build exists. Any version outside the line fails closed.

capability.note: The agent-to-sandbox path a user actually mounts: the agent authors a module and its sidecar, hands the registry directory to the stdio server, and the OFFICIAL MCP Python SDK client registers and executes it. The same session pins the boundary — a sidecar asking for /etc gets no preopen (allow_dirs_configured stays visible, security_baseline.preopens stays ['/sandbox']) and the guest finds no handle, and a module that never returns is stopped by the fuel budget as an isError result. CI-gated in mcp-sdk-interop, which is why it is 'supported' rather than 'experimental'.

capability.reason: A LangGraph StateGraph and a LangChain tool were executed against the real SDKs and the core wheel (benchmarks/results/2026-10-14/agent_frameworks.json), but the autonomous model-driven loop is reported skipped, not faked, and the adapter is not CI-gated.
Import and node validity are measured; the agent-driven end-to-end loop through n8n's own client is not proven.
The composite action and its demo workflow are defined, but no workflow of this candidate has executed on a GitHub-hosted runner.
Ephemora Enterprise is a separate private product. No Enterprise source, capability or configuration is part of this package or this contract.

`ephemora run --backend vm` runs the job inside a Linux VM created through Apple Virtualization.framework on macOS 15+ arm64, with the module or script streamed over a digest-bound `hvc1` channel and host actions gated by a host mediator; tenant attribution and a tenant book are mandatory and unsupported flags are refused instead of ignored. The contract tests run on every platform, and real runs on the qualified machine cover all three guest languages. It is experimental, not supported, because the VM assets (kernel, initramfs, probe) are third-party or locally built binaries that this source release does not carry: redistribution clearance for them is an open release gate, so a fresh install cannot build a VM guest by itself.

A VM run cannot produce a signed execution record yet. The CLI refuses `--evidence` on the VM path rather than writing an unsigned file that looks like an attestation, and the record marks a VM run `host_verified: false` because fuel and output come from the guest, not from the host. A minimal host-side execution record for the VM path is the open item.

The MCP tool surface executes on the native worker only. Nothing in the server reaches the VM backend, so an MCP run must not be described as VM-isolated; wiring and qualifying that path is separate work.

capability.note: `ephemora tenant usage` reads a 1.1.0 book; `ephemora tenant migrate` writes a booking_version=2 copy carrying runs, charges, violations, refusals, recovered runs and the six conservative-booking counters, then re-reads and verifies what it carried. Legacy books remain readable and are never written; a book mixing stamped and unstamped settlements is refused as stripped-version tampering.

capability.reason: Linux stays in the product strategy as an isolation backend, not as a claim. On the tested Linux host the OS-level isolation probe did not establish the expected boundary (unprivileged user namespaces were not available to the harness), and no qualified build of the release runtime exists for Linux, so no isolation profile is advertised there. The platform gate is open work, not a reason to reposition the product as macOS-only.
